name: Azerbaijan
summary: Light blue, red and green horizontal bands with a white crescent and eight-pointed star in the red band. Adopted by the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic in 1918, it was restored in 1991.
origin: The Azerbaijan Democratic Republic, the first parliamentary republic in the Muslim world, adopted this tricolour on 9 November 1918. After the Soviet takeover in 1920 it was replaced by the flags of the Azerbaijan SSR.
The tricolour was used by the opposition from the late 1980s, adopted by the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic in 1990, and restored as the national flag on 5 February 1991.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: Progress and the building of a modern, democratic state.

symbols.name: Crescent and eight-pointed star
symbols.description: A white crescent with an eight-pointed star to its right, in the red band.
symbols.meaning: The crescent is linked to Islam; the eight points are often said to represent the eight Turkic peoples, or the eight letters of the name 'Azerbaijan' in the Arabic script.

facts: The National Flag Square in Baku held one of the tallest flagpoles in the world when it opened in 2010.
National Flag Day is 9 November, the anniversary of the 1918 adoption.
The three colours are often summarised as 'Turkify, Modernise, Islamise', a slogan of the writer Ali bey Huseynzade.
clues: Light blue, red and green bands with a white crescent and eight-pointed star.
First adopted by the first parliamentary republic in the Muslim world, in 1918.
